elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets."

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly covers "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" without HDI's consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent".

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...which shall not be unreasonably withheld" attaches directly to the Company's consent to HDI assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "and may not in any event assign to a competitor of the Company" — absolute bar, not consent-gated.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "A change of control of the Company shall not give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement." No contrary change-of-control trigger appears in the cited or surrounding termination language.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: HDI's assignment (including to a successor) is gated on the Company's prior written consent; the insertion gives no reciprocal free successor-assignment right to HDI.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no notice obligation for the Company's affiliate/successor assignments.

The Company retains a no-consent affiliate exception (a non-successor exception), so not all other assignments are consent-gated; nor is any consent gate stated for the Company's remaining assignments.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Reasonableness standard is stated for the only consent gate created ("shall not be unreasonably withheld"); condition applies asymmetrically but is satisfied where consent is required.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language: Customer affiliate and M&A-successor assignment without consent, a consent gate on Vendor assignment with a reasonableness standard, an absolute competitor bar, and an express statement that Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right. The position is complete at the preferred level.

Fallback is incomplete (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and the retained Customer affiliate exception defeats "Other assignments require consent"), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully satisfied.

Minimality holds: the existing successors-and-assigns sentence is retained verbatim, one concise paragraph is inserted for a clause that previously had no assignment mechanics, and nothing outside the checklist (no survival tail, expense, notice-procedure or damages boilerplate) is added. The change-of-control sentence is a listed preferred element, not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the retained sentence continues to bind and benefit "successors and assigns" and does not contradict the new permitted transfers; the insertion introduces no undefined terms or dangling cross-references, and does not create a new Vendor assignment exception.

Optional polish only (not required for completeness): consider confirming that a permitted assignee is not an "other person" excluded by the final words of the retained sentence, to remove any argument of tension.
